analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING 1) FX Trader Call Today, 2) Midterms Review, 3) QRA Preview, 4) CNY Update and 5) COPOM Preview 4 Nov 2026
key_insights: Privorotsky (Head of EMEA Flow Intermediation and European One Delta Trading) argues AI infrastructure has been oversold after the midterms. Electoral uncertainty has diminished, positioning looks cleaner, and he expects vol to come in quickly and drive spot higher in the short term.

The AI data centre debate has shifted from the cost of compute to whether capacity can be permitted, energized and delivered in 2027-2029. Moratoriums, local opposition and a possibly more restrictive regulatory environment could constrain supply.

Constrained data centre supply is potentially negative for chip, cooling and electrical equipment sellers, because customers may have overordered relative to capacity they can energize. Privorotsky says much of that risk appears reflected in multiples.

Constrained supply raises the scarcity value of existing, energized compute, which potentially benefits hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity. Neoclouds are split between those with existing compute and contracted demand and those dependent on new facilities, financing and power.

GS Rates Strategy (Marshall) expects Treasury at the QRA to keep 10-to-30y coupon auction sizes steady and maintain or modestly increase buyback envelope sizes. A cut in long-end auction sizes is a risk but not the base case.

GS expects Treasury to adjust its guidance to signal potential auction size changes, with two-sided language, and to begin raising 2-to-7y auction sizes in May 2027. Auction sizes are expected to stay unchanged through 1Q27.

GS says market expectations likely lean toward reduced long-end auction sizes, leaving scope for disappointment and long-end underperformance on the spread curve. The impact should be somewhat contained because Treasury is unlikely to undo prior measures.
GS fair value models show long-end spreads wide to fair value and a somewhat steep spread curve. Longer-term forwards are only modestly above fair value.

GS EM FX (Mediratta): USDCNY onshore fixing was 6.7180 versus 6.7150 the day before, the largest one-day increase since Aug 18. GS reads it as reinforcing the signal from the FX RRR hike that the PBOC is targeting the pace of appreciation.

USDCNH bounced to a high of 6.6855 and was sold as the broader USD weakened after the Democratic sweep in US elections. The gap between USDCNH and the onshore fixing traded as low as -700 before moving to about -450.

GS expects the USDCNH path lower to continue, supported by a rising trade surplus, exporter conversions and RMB internationalization, with possible US-China meetings around APEC and the G20. A fix 200-300 pips from the lows would signal a definite change in intent.

GS LatAm Economics (Ramos) expects the BCB to hold the Selic at 13.75% and pause the easing cycle at COPOM. Reasons: worse inflation outlook, weaker BRL, a deteriorating budget baseline after campaign fiscal commitments, and a dimmer outlook for a near-term fiscal anchor.

GS puts a 25bp cut to 13.50% at 30% probability, paired with firm guidance setting a high bar for a December cut. Forward guidance is expected to signal a pause rather than a definitive end to the cycle.

GS BRL Rates Trading (Fonseca) also expects a hold after five consecutive 25bp cuts. Last Friday's market close priced about a 25% chance of a 25bp cut via Digital Options, with about 170bp of hikes priced through Jan28.

tension_points.bull_case: Constrained supply raises the scarcity value of existing, energized compute, benefiting hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity. Throttled supply could push pricing higher for longer rather than destroy demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Customers may have overordered chips, cooling and electrical equipment relative to capacity they can energize, which is negative for picks and shovels. Neoclouds dependent on new facilities, financing and power are exposed.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects unchanged 10-to-30y auction sizes and steady or modestly higher buybacks, since a reduction seems unnecessary on liquidity or demand grounds.
tension_points.bear_case: Market expectations lean toward reduced long-end auction sizes, so unchanged sizes could disappoint and cause long-end underperformance on the spread curve.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut in long-end auction sizes would invalidate the GS base case.

tension_points.bull_case: A 25bp cut to 13.50% with firm guidance is possible (GS 30%), and activity has continued to lose momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation above target, worse expectations, higher oil, BRL weakness and fiscal deterioration make a cut hard to justify, so GS expects a hold at 13.75%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 25bp cut to 13.50% at the COPOM decision would invalidate the GS hold call.
